title: President Trump Kennedy Center Name Judge Order
report:
**Summary:** A federal judge has ruled that President Trump's name cannot be added to the John F. Kennedy Center in Washington D.C., citing a law that prohibits any changes to the center's name without Congressional approval. The judge also temporarily blocked plans to close the center for two years of renovations, calling them "murky." The ruling was made in response to a lawsuit filed by Rep. Joyce Beatty, an ex-officio member of the Kennedy Center board. The Kennedy Center has announced that it will appeal the decision.

**5 Key Facts:**

1. **Judge's Ruling:** U.S. District Court Judge Christopher Cooper ruled that President Trump's name cannot be added to the John F. Kennedy Center, citing a law that prohibits any changes to the center's name without Congressional approval.
2. **Renovation Plans Blocked:** The judge also temporarily blocked plans to close the center for two years of renovations, calling them "murky" and stating that board members did not have sufficient information to make a well-considered decision.
3. **Lawsuit Background:** The ruling was made in response to a lawsuit filed by Rep. Joyce Beatty, an ex-officio member of the Kennedy Center board whose voting rights were stripped last year.
4. **Kennedy Center Response:** A spokesperson for the Kennedy Center announced that it will appeal the decision and remains committed to pursuing renovations with $257 million secured by President Trump and approved by Congress.
5. **Removal of Signage:** The judge ordered that all signage and online materials referring to the "Donald J. Trump and John F. Kennedy Memorial Center for the Performing Arts" or similar names must be removed within 14 days.
